story.title: The Grain Mountain at Wuchao
story.text: All of Yuan Shao's grain was stored at Wuchao, piled like a hill.
story.narration: At Guandu the two armies faced each other. Cao Cao had few soldiers and little food, while cart after cart of Yuan Shao's grain rolled into Wuchao and piled up like a hill. Yuan Shao could afford to wait; Cao Cao could not.

story.title: Burning the Grain at Night
story.text: Cao Cao did not fight head-on: he slipped into Wuchao at night and burned the grain.
story.narration: Cao Cao did not throw his men against Yuan Shao's army. He picked a small band of picked troops, took up torches, crept into Wuchao in the dark and burned the granaries. With the grain gone, Yuan Shao's great army could not hold on.

keyMoment.question: Yuan Shao has more men and more grain. Where do you strike?

options.text: Gather everyone and charge his army head-on
options.hint: He has more men and more grain — we cannot outlast him.

options.text: Burn the grain at Wuchao — that is what holds him up
Pull back and wait for him to grow weak
options.hint: His grain carts keep rolling while we wait.

keyMoment.reveal: Do not beat at the flames — pull the firewood out from under them, and the fire goes out by itself.

misconceptions: A big fire can only be beaten with a bigger effort
If you cannot win, step aside and wait

quiz.question: Where was Yuan Shao's grain stored?
quiz.explanation: All the grain was at Wuchao — that is the place Cao Cao burned at night.

quiz.question: The soup is too salty and adding water does not help. What is smarter?
options: Put in less salt — fix it at the root
quiz.explanation: More water leaves the saltiness in the pot; using less salt is pulling the firewood out from under the fire.
